item.title: Two men in late teens pronounced dead in Ballina collision
item.description: Gardaí are appealing for witnesses following a fatal collision in Ballina, Co. Mayo. The incident involving one vehicle happened in the early hours of this morning. Gardaí and emergency services attended the scene on a local road (L5140) at Laghtadawannagh near Ballina. Two of the car's occupants, both adult males in their late teens, were pronounced deceased. item.title: Nursing home in Co. Leitrim receives positive HIQA report
item.description: A county Leitrim nursing home has received a largely positive report from the health watchdog. HIQA carried out an unannounced inspection of Lough Erril Private Nursing Home close to Mohill in November last year, the details of which have been published this week. Lough Erril admits and provides care for residents of varying degrees of dependency, from low to maximum. The nursing home is over two levels. All resident accommodation is on the ground floor. item.title: People in Co. Leitrim encouraged to take part in national frog survey
item.description: People in County Leitrim are being encouraged to take part in a national frog survey. The 'Hop To It' survey has been carried out by the Irish Peatland Conservation Council since 1997. Leitrim County Council is now asking residents across the county to play their part in this citizen science initiative. item.description: Leitrim were caught flat footed as Tipperary scored a decisive 13-point win in Clonmel. item.title: Kate O'Connor leaps to national indoor championship record
item.description: Kate O’Connor, who produced one of the standout performances of the national indoor championships in the women’s long jump. O’Connor’s opening-round leap of 6.50m was not only a personal best, but also a championship record. That jump moved O’Connor to third on the Irish all-time list. It also capped a remarkable weekend following her personal best run in the 60m hurdles (8.21) on Saturday.
